§3 · The £ engine

The real fair.py

First 40 lines of the actual engine — no dependencies, beta-PERT via stdlib, seed-deterministic.

fair.py
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""fair.py — lightweight, deterministic FAIR risk engine (pure stdlib, offline).
 
Turns versioned (min, mode, max) risk triples into an annual-loss distribution and
reads the board numbers off it: ALE, VaR95, TVaR, and the £ actually carried
(TVaR + a risk load, so the balance sheet never charges the mean).
 
This is the load-bearing seam for the whole risk thesis: the "£ moves when you
tighten a control" beat is two invocations of this CLI differing by one input.
 
Deps: none. beta-PERT is sampled via random.betavariate (stdlib Mersenne Twister,
deterministic and portable across platforms given a fixed seed).
 
Usage:
    fair.py summary   scenarios/driftwood-cart-pii.json [--mode warn|deny]
    fair.py compare   scenarios/driftwood-cart-pii.json     # what a Deny buys
    fair.py selfcheck                                        # runnable asserts
 
Scenario JSON (versioned triples):
    { "version": "v1", "name": "...",
      "warn": {"lef": [min,mode,max], "lm": [min,mode,max]},
      "deny": {"lef": [min,mode,max], "lm": [min,mode,max]} }
  or a single unnamed control state:
    { "version": "v1", "name": "...", "lef": [...], "lm": [...] }
"""
from __future__ import annotations
 
import argparse
import json
import random
import sys
 
# Defaults. ponytail: PERT lambda fixed at 4 (standard FAIR confidence); cost-of-
# capital fixed at Solvency-II's 6% risk-margin rate. Expose per-scenario only if
# an estimator actually needs to widen/narrow either.
ITERATIONS = 10_000
SEED = 42
PERT_LAMBDA = 4.0
COST_OF_CAPITAL = 0.06  # risk load = COC * economic capital (TVaR - ALE)
§4

The money-shot

One control, one scenario, one £ figure — and two appetites give two verdicts. Proportionality by comparison, not by opinion.

§4 · The money-shot

Same control, same £, two verdicts

risk_bought £21,107: driftwood's £40k band renders Audit, ludlow's £5k band renders Deny. Same body, the £ picks.

proportionality
==> 0. the £ engine's own asserts (band selection, tightening raises £, no timer)
ok  driftwood(£40000 tol): loose buys £19439 -> Audit | tightened buys £54520 -> Deny | same loose under ludlow(£5000 tol) -> Deny
==> 1. the SAME control + SAME scenario -> divergent £-derived verdicts
==> 2. the £ that DRIVES it — same risk_bought, different appetite band
    risk_bought £21,107  |  driftwood band £40,000 -> Audit  |  ludlow band £5,000 -> Deny
==> 3. the rendered policies carry the £-derived action (not hand-authored)
ok  committed policies match the £-derived render for driftwood, ludlow
==> 4. the shared control body is a real, self-scoping policy (pass/fail/unversioned)
==> 5. live(driftwood): cluster reachable but Kyverno CRDs not installed — skipping dry-run (offline proof stands)
==> 5. live(ludlow): cluster reachable but Kyverno CRDs not installed — skipping dry-run (offline proof stands)
==> 5. live dry-run tail skipped (no cluster with Kyverno CRDs reachable) — offline proof stands
PASS: same control, same £ (risk_bought £21107) — Audit in driftwood, Deny in ludlow. Proportionality by comparison.

§4 · The money-shot

The orphan-guard

Only versions the array declares can run: 3.0.0 (undeclared) is denied, 1.0.0 admits. The allow-list IS the array.

orphan-guard
==> 1. render the orphan-guard from the version array (declares 1.0.0, 2.0.0)
==> 2. an undeclared version (3.0.0) is denied; a declared one (1.0.0) admits
PASS: only versions the array declares can run; the allow-list is the array.
§5

Graded + TCoR

Behind-posture workloads aren't denied — they're caged by degree. The board line is Total Cost of Risk, and it moves as the levers predict.

§5 · Graded + TCoR

§8 · Identity

The fixed HelmRelease

Chart 0.24.0 camelCased its values with hard fail() guards; the corrected values that let SPIRE install.

spire/helmrelease.yaml
        trustDomain: acme.internal
        # k8s_psat node attestation is the chart default; kept explicit for the talk.
    spire-server:
      # spire-controller-manager reconciles ClusterSPIFFEID -> registration entries
      # (gcInterval ~10s), so posture-label changes drop an entry within ~10s.
      controllerManager:
        enabled: true
      # Short TTLs = snappy revocation for the live "loses reach in minutes" beat.
      # JWT 5m so an out-of-currency caller loses its OpenBao secret fast (research 16 Q4).
      caSubject: { country: [UK], organization: [acme], commonName: acme.internal }
    spire-agent:
      # Agent socket exposed on-host so Istio's Envoy can pull SVIDs over the
      # SPIFFE Workload API (SDS). Path must match Istio's caAddress below.
      socketPath: /run/spire/agent-sockets/spire-agent.sock
    spiffe-csi-driver:
      # Mounts the agent socket read-only into meshed pods (the Istio+SPIRE path).
      enabled: true
    spiffe-oidc-discovery-provider:
      # JWKS endpoint OpenBao's jwt auth validates JWT-SVIDs against (research 16 Q4).
      enabled: true
